definitions.explanation: Reading only selected parts of a text rather than the whole thing, picking out what seems interesting or relevant. Literally 'picking-up reading.'

examples.japanese: {新聞|しんぶん}を{拾|ひろ}い{読|よ}みした。
{時間|じかん}がなくて{拾|ひろ}い{読|よ}みしかできなかった。
examples.english: I didn't have time and could only skim through it.

examples.japanese: {報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{拾|ひろ}い{読|よ}みして、{重要|じゅうよう}な{部分|ぶぶん}だけ{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I skimmed the report and checked only the important parts.

notes:
USAGE:
Suggests a quick, selective style of reading rather than careful, thorough reading. Not necessarily negative — sometimes practical when short on time. Can be used with する as a verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {拾|ひろ}い{読|よ}みする (to skim, to browse)
- {拾|ひろ}い{読|よ}みしかできない (can only skim)
- ざっと{拾|ひろ}い{読|よ}みする (to quickly skim through)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {斜|なな}め{読|よ}み: speed-reading, skimming — similar meaning, literally 'diagonal reading'
- {流|なが}し{読|よ}み: cursory reading — reading quickly without focusing
